sentences.show: On a Friday the 13th, at dawn, a king arrested an order of knights "as rich as kings".
It happened on this day in 1307.
King Philip IV of France was deeply in debt to the Knights Templar.
A month earlier, he had sent secret orders across his kingdom.
At dawn, his soldiers seized every Templar they could find, all at once.
The charges: spitting on the cross, and worshipping a bearded head.
In Paris, under torture, almost all of them confessed.
In 1312, the Pope dissolved the order.
In 1314, Grand Master Jacques de Molay took back his confession.
He was burned on an island in the Seine.
A witness said he told the crowd that God would avenge them.
Within a year, the Pope and the King were both dead.
Some say this is where the fear of Friday the 13th began. The truth is murkier.
Also on this day: the Miracle of the Sun at Fátima, and thirty-three miners rescued after sixty-nine days.
Like those sealed orders, our app awaits its dawn. Subscribe, and be there when it opens.
